name: Graffiti / Street Art
visualIdentity: Supplemental reference, not a directly named source-collection style. Combines spray-painted lettering, tags, wall texture, and street graphics in a coherent lettering style and palette. Use selective overspray and layered paint; keep the principal message recognizable.
suitableUses: Explicit combinations suit lettering-led pieces, music promos, event teasers, and culture explainers with brief flyer inserts. Inferred suitability: bold product or editorial introductions and illustrated narratives where street graphics support the subject. Works alone for lettering-focused pieces.
limitations: Avoid random overspray, excessive layers or flyer inserts, mixed palettes, and effects that make the message hard to read. These constraints are explicit for the suggested hybrids; broader limits are unspecified. The palette below is a suggestion, not a canonical definition.
palette: Suggested tokens for new artwork only: background #E7E1D4, foreground #272631, accents #BC4861, #388A8B, #CEA248; discrete colors, no gradient. Use exact task, brand, or approved reference colors first and preserve their roles and asset colors. The supplied foreground/background pair has contrast 11.449; accent pairs vary, so check actual compositing and place body text on a suitable backing.
motionAndInteraction: Reveal strokes, overpaint areas, and replace graphic layers while controlling paint coverage and stroke movement over time. Use seeded spray brushes and path masks; prepare tags separately from main lettering. For video, derive state from seekable composition time. Interactive HTML may map finite scroll progress to chapter handoffs or story steps, with synchronized copy, readable holds, and coherent backward states. These are optional narrative patterns, not required effects.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory layer. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and explicit audio requirements. Beat-synced stroke reveals are suggested for music promos, but not every stroke should hit a beat. Use authorized assets and check speech clarity, balance, clipping, and picture sync.
assetRequirements: Prepare tags and main lettering as separate layers; use suitable wall texture, street graphics, fonts, and any supplied exact copy or artwork. combinations: Style-105 may support music-timed reveals: keep the primary spray palette and message legible; avoid random overspray and over-layering. HyperFrames owns composition, timing, audio sync, validation, and export; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified required capability is blocked, and record why.
